issues.summary: [PROJECT-GUIDE] Agent execution contract, readiness gate and delivery order
issues.actor: Product owner and architecture reviewer
issues.outcome: A versioned Jira catalog prevents generic or incomplete tickets from being dispatched and synchronizes managed Jira fields without rewriting completed history or workflow state.
issues.context: The v1.2 catalog covered every issue but generated broad acceptance text and synthetic permissions. Catalog v1.3 makes semantic readiness enforceable, shards specifications by epic, and adds canary-only synchronization plus an explicit promotion gate.
inScope: Compile all v1.3 epic shards into one deterministic 401-record catalog and reject duplicate Source-IDs or Jira keys.
Reject executable leaves that lack concrete repository paths, artifacts, authorization actions, AC-to-test mapping, reproducible commands, or refined parents.
Synchronize descriptions, labels, Module, parents, issue types, and typed dependency links with backup, optimistic concurrency, canary limits, and no implicit creation or workflow transition.
outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.
Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: A decision is publishable only after named owner approval, effective time, supersession rule, fixtures, and rollback impact are recorded.
Example values are DRAFT/UAT only unless an explicit production policy is maker-checker approved.

contracts.name: Atlassian Jira Cloud REST API v3
contracts.compatibility: Use Source-ID and Jira key identity, preserve comments, worklogs, attachments, sprint and status, and abort on concurrent updated timestamps.

contracts.name: ViStay Jira catalog v1.3 JSON schema
contracts.compatibility: v1.2 stays immutable; v1.3 is compiled from per-epic shards and validated before synchronization.

interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Versioned policy and decision records are owned by platform_contracts; runtime services consume published versions and never silently invent defaults.
stateMachine: Specification moves from needs-refinement or decision-required to executable only after semantic validation; executable leaves become agent-ready or agent-ready-after-dependencies from live dependency state.
Jira workflow transitions are never performed by catalog synchronization; Ready promotion and Backlog demotion use the separate promotion gate.
Completed Jira issues are historical and their descriptions remain immutable; remediation is represented by a new Bug or Tech Debt issue.

dataPartitions: PROJECT:SCRUM only; credentials must have explicit project permission and may not enumerate other Jira projects.
fieldGroups: DELIVERY_SPEC is managed from the catalog; WORKFLOW_EVIDENCE, COMMENTS, ATTACHMENTS, WORKLOGS, SPRINT and STATUS remain Jira-owned.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

acceptanceCriteria.given: the 26 v1.3 source shards containing all managed project issues
acceptanceCriteria.when: npm run validate:jira is executed in platform_contracts
acceptanceCriteria.then: one deterministic 401-record catalog is built, all Jira keys are present, and structural plus semantic validation succeeds

acceptanceCriteria.given: an open issue still contains generator boilerplate or lacks a concrete path, artifact, authorization action, AC mapping, or command
acceptanceCriteria.when: that issue is marked executable or dispatchable
acceptanceCriteria.then: validation fails and the issue cannot receive agent-ready

acceptanceCriteria.given: a reviewed catalog and a fresh Jira backup
acceptanceCriteria.when: a canary Apply is requested for at most five Source-IDs
acceptanceCriteria.then: only those issues are updated, any concurrent Jira edit aborts the run, no workflow status changes, and a repeated selected DryRun reports zero changes

tests: Catalog build and semantic validation cover identity, hierarchy, readiness, repository, authorization, acceptance, test-command, and evidence invariants.
Jira Validate and DryRun cover credential access, catalog-to-live identity, Module options, typed links, managed-field drift, backup, and reviewable plan generation.
Canary Apply plus selected zero-diff DryRun proves idempotent synchronization without touching Jira-owned workflow evidence.

testCases.evidence: platform_contracts console output showing 401 valid records, readiness counts, zero unsafe dispatchable records, and zero missing Jira keys
timestamped Jira backup and JSON dry-run plan for SCRUM-537
Apply result followed by a selected DryRun with changes=0 and unchanged Jira workflow status

observability: Propagate trace and correlation IDs across GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/webhook boundaries without logging secrets or protected fields.
Emit transition, latency, error-code, replay/deduplication, dependency, and repair-queue metrics with bounded-cardinality labels.
Provide dashboard/alert thresholds and a runbook for stuck states, reconciliation mismatch, and rollback.
definitionOfDone: Catalog validation and all affected repository CI checks pass.
Contracts, migrations, compatibility path, implementation, Admin Web/Mobile parity where applicable, and Postman/Newman evidence are merged.
Security-negative, concurrency/replay, observability, reconciliation, and rollback evidence is linked in Jira.
No production secret or unapproved monetary/policy default is committed; ServiceOwner acceptance evidence is attached before Done.
evidence: Pull request and commit links per repository.
Automated test and Newman report with fixture version.
Migration/rollback or compatibility evidence where data/contracts change.
Dashboard, trace, audit, and reconciliation screenshots or machine-readable artifacts.
issues.decisionNoteVi: Các quy tắc nghiệp vụ và ranh giới dữ liệu trong catalog v1.2 đã được chốt; thay đổi sau này phải tạo phiên bản policy/contract mới, không sửa ngược lịch sử.

issues.summary: [VS-E03-S01-ST01] Implement authorized presigned upload sessions
issues.actor: Authorized backoffice operator or trusted ViStay service
issues.outcome: Media Service creates a bounded upload session and returns private, short-lived presigned upload instructions only after action, partition, file-count, type, and size authorization succeeds.
issues.context: The baseline migration already contains upload_sessions and media_assets. Implement the missing domain/application/persistence/object-store adapters and GraphQL mutation without moving binary content into PostgreSQL.
inScope: Add authorizeMediaUpload GraphQL input/payload and stable error mapping.
Validate 1..20 files, per-file JPEG/PNG/WebP <=15 MiB or PDF <=25 MiB, total <=100 MiB, sanitized filenames, and session expiry.
Persist PENDING upload session/assets and generate private object keys and presigned PUT URLs with content-type and checksum constraints.
Write audit and outbox rows in the creation transaction.
outOfScope: Frontend rendering outside the owning service contract.
Direct reads from another service database.
Production credentials, destructive history rewrites, or silent fallback authorization.
businessRules: Allow JPEG/PNG/WebP up to 15 MiB and PDF up to 25 MiB; one session allows at most 20 files and 100 MiB.
Reject video, SVG, Office, and HEIC initially; verify magic bytes, malware status, checksum, and strip image EXIF.
Upload/download URLs are short lived and objects remain private.
interfaces: Expose only the operations named in this issue through the owning GraphQL or gRPC boundary.
Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, and dependency-unavailable codes.
Persist an outbox event in the same transaction for every externally observable state change.
dataOwnership: Media owns upload sessions, object metadata, checksum, scan state, retention state, access audit, and domain references; object bytes stay in private object storage.
stateMachine: Upload session begins PENDING and may issue URLs only until expiresAt.
The first accepted object transfer advances the session to UPLOADING; authorization alone does not mark content uploaded.
Expired or cancelled sessions cannot issue another URL; retries with the same idempotency key return the original session.

dataPartitions: ADMIN organization plus SITE/BRANCH membership for the target property; SYSTEM is limited to authenticated internal repair or projection calls.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY is baseline; DOCUMENT and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit field-group grants.

failureSemantics: Reject malformed or unauthorized calls before mutating state and do not reveal whether a restricted aggregate exists.
Map stale expectedVersion to CONFLICT_STALE_REVISION and unavailable required dependencies to DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE.
Retry only object-store, scanner, or event-publication failures classified as transient; retain the failed job for bounded repair.
idempotencyConcurrency: Require an idempotency key for commands that can be retried externally and persist its request fingerprint and result.
Use aggregate version compare-and-swap so concurrent writers produce one winner and a stable conflict for losers.
Deduplicate consumed events by event ID and business key.

issues.actor: Authorized backoffice operator or trusted ViStay service
issues.outcome: Media Service verifies uploaded bytes by object metadata, magic bytes, declared type, size, and SHA-256, then drives malware and metadata processing to AVAILABLE or a visible terminal failure.
issues.context: Finalize is a command over an existing non-expired upload session. Object-store HEAD/read-range and malware scanning are dependency ports; scan failure must never publish the asset as available.
inScope: Add finalizeMediaUpload with expectedVersion and idempotency key.
Verify object presence, ETag where available, SHA-256, size, MIME magic bytes, and the allowed-type policy.
Create replay-safe VERIFY_UPLOAD, MALWARE_SCAN, STRIP_METADATA, and thumbnail jobs; strip image EXIF.
Advance PENDING_UPLOAD -> UPLOADED -> PROCESSING -> AVAILABLE, QUARANTINED, or FAILED with audit/outbox evidence.
outOfScope: Frontend rendering outside the owning service contract.
Direct reads from another service database.
Production credentials, destructive history rewrites, or silent fallback authorization.
businessRules: Allow JPEG/PNG/WebP up to 15 MiB and PDF up to 25 MiB; one session allows at most 20 files and 100 MiB.
Reject video, SVG, Office, and HEIC initially; verify magic bytes, malware status, checksum, and strip image EXIF.
Upload/download URLs are short lived and objects remain private.
interfaces: Expose only the operations named in this issue through the owning GraphQL or gRPC boundary.
Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, and dependency-unavailable codes.

stateMachine: Only PENDING_UPLOAD may finalize; object verification moves it to UPLOADED and queued processing moves it to PROCESSING.
Clean scan plus successful metadata stripping produces AVAILABLE; infected content produces QUARANTINED.
Dependency exhaustion produces FAILED with repair metadata; a repair retry cannot skip a required successful scan.

dataPartitions: ADMIN organization plus SITE/BRANCH membership for the target property; SYSTEM is limited to authenticated internal repair or projection calls.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY is baseline; DOCUMENT and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit field-group grants.

failureSemantics: Reject malformed or unauthorized calls before mutating state and do not reveal whether a restricted aggregate exists.

Use aggregate version compare-and-swap so concurrent writers produce one winner and a stable conflict for losers.
Deduplicate consumed events by event ID and business key.

issues.summary: [VS-E06] Unified Inventory & Availability
issues.actor: Booking agent and inventory reconciler
issues.outcome: Completed inventory service, contract, Postman, and Admin Web work remain historical; the remaining Admin Mobile parity Task is the only dispatchable leaf.
issues.context: The Epic coordinates historical evidence plus the open mobile consumer without rewriting Done descriptions.
inScope: Implement and verify: Unified Inventory & Availability.
Version contract, persistence, authorization, failure, audit, and operator behavior needed by this outcome.
Provide repository-specific automated tests and Postman/Newman evidence for callable APIs.
outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.
Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: Availability uses half-open intervals and exact units.
Mutating commands require idempotency key and expected revision; overlap is rejected under concurrency.
Expired/orphan blocks are reconciled without deleting audit history.
interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Booking owns exact-unit holds, reservation occupancy, and inventory-block projection; maintenance sources publish blocking facts.
stateMachine: Model legal states and transitions for Unified Inventory & Availability; reject illegal transitions with stable error codes.
Persist actor, reason, source, policy/contract version, expected revision, and timestamps for every material transition.
Terminal or superseded records are retained; corrections use a new revision or compensating record.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM for internal repair only; otherwise enforce the subject account type and the resource customer, host-party, site, branch, or assigned-employee partition.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; FINANCIAL, PII, DOCUMENT, TRUST_DETAIL, and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit grants and response-field filtering.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an authorized actor with a valid partition and a complete request for Unified Inventory & Availability
acceptanceCriteria.when: the command or query is executed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the documented outcome, state revision, audit record, and contract response are produced deterministically

acceptanceCriteria.given: a caller missing the action, partition, or requested field-group grant
acceptanceCriteria.then: access is denied without leaking existence or restricted fields and the denial is auditable

acceptanceCriteria.given: the same mutation is replayed or two requests use the same expected revision
acceptanceCriteria.then: at most one business effect is committed and all responses are stable, explainable, and reconciled

tests: Unit tests cover rule boundaries, legal/illegal transitions, rounding/timezone where relevant, and stable error mapping.
Integration tests cover persistence constraints, authorization action+partition+field groups, outbox/inbox replay, and dependency failure.
Postman/Newman flow covers happy path, negative authorization, validation, conflict, idempotent replay, and a cleanup-safe deterministic fixture.
observability: Propagate trace and correlation IDs across GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/webhook boundaries without logging secrets or protected fields.
Emit transition, latency, error-code, replay/deduplication, dependency, and repair-queue metrics with bounded-cardinality labels.
Provide dashboard/alert thresholds and a runbook for stuck states, reconciliation mismatch, and rollback.
definitionOfDone: Catalog validation and all affected repository CI checks pass.
Contracts, migrations, compatibility path, implementation, Admin Web/Mobile parity where applicable, and Postman/Newman evidence are merged.
Security-negative, concurrency/replay, observability, reconciliation, and rollback evidence is linked in Jira.
No production secret or unapproved monetary/policy default is committed; ServiceOwner acceptance evidence is attached before Done.
evidence: Pull request and commit links per repository.
Automated test and Newman report with fixture version.
Migration/rollback or compatibility evidence where data/contracts change.
Dashboard, trace, audit, and reconciliation screenshots or machine-readable artifacts.

issues.summary: [VS-E07-S01-ST01] Implement privacy-safe lead capture and duplicate hints
issues.actor: Authorized backoffice operator or trusted ViStay service
issues.outcome: Booking Service captures a privacy-safe pre-customer lead and returns partition-filtered duplicate hints without automatically merging people or claiming that a lead is a User profile.
issues.context: No lead table or CRM API currently exists. Create an additive V10 model using encrypted contact display values and keyed normalized lookup hashes; do not log or expose raw PII in events.
inScope: Add lead_contacts with encrypted name/phone/email, HMAC lookup hashes, consent/source metadata, linked customerProfileId reference, owner/branch, lifecycle, revision, and configured retention class.
Add createLead, updateLeadContact, linkLeadToCustomer, lead, and searchLeads GraphQL operations with cursor pagination and expectedVersion.
Generate exact/near duplicate hints from normalized hashes and bounded non-PII signals; require explicit authorized merge/link action and preserve both histories.
Write redacted audit/outbox records and support configured anonymization without deleting financial/booking references.
outOfScope: Frontend rendering outside the owning service contract.
Direct reads from another service database.
Production credentials, destructive history rewrites, or silent fallback authorization.
businessRules: Lead PII is purpose-limited and duplicate hints never auto-merge people.
A request does not consume inventory until an explicit hold succeeds.
Assignment, stage, loss reason, source, campaign, and responsible employee are audited.
interfaces: Expose only the operations named in this issue through the owning GraphQL or gRPC boundary.
Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, and dependency-unavailable codes.
Persist an outbox event in the same transaction for every externally observable state change.
dataOwnership: Booking owns pre-customer lead contact envelopes, inquiries, booking requests, attribution, follow-up, quote/hold references, and their lifecycle audit. User owns account/customer profile identity; Booking stores only its stable reference after linkage.
stateMachine: Lead is NEW -> ACTIVE -> CONVERTED or CLOSED; configured anonymization changes contact fields to ANONYMIZED without removing references/audit.
Duplicate hint is advisory and never changes identity or ownership.
Linking to a User customer profile is explicit, revision-checked, and immutable except through an audited unlink/correction command.

dataPartitions: ADMIN organization plus assigned EMPLOYEE_SELF/TEAM or SITE/BRANCH scope derived from the request; SYSTEM is restricted to authenticated internal repair.
fieldGroups: CRM_SUMMARY is baseline; PII_CONTACT, CRM_ATTRIBUTION, FINANCIAL, and INTERNAL_AUDIT each require an explicit field-group grant.

failureSemantics: Reject invalid or unauthorized CRM commands before persisting PII or lifecycle changes and never reveal duplicate candidates outside the caller partition.
Map duplicate idempotency key mismatch, stale revision, invalid transition, inventory conflict, and dependency failure to distinct stable codes.
Retry only transient customer-reference, authorization, outbox, or inventory dependencies; never retry a business conflict as a new command.
idempotencyConcurrency: Require an idempotency key for commands that can be retried externally and persist its request fingerprint and result.
Use aggregate version compare-and-swap so concurrent writers produce one winner and a stable conflict for losers.
Deduplicate consumed events by event ID and business key.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an authorized employee submits valid contact data and consent/source metadata
acceptanceCriteria.then: one encrypted lead with lookup hashes, owner partition, audit/outbox evidence, and redacted duplicate hints is returned

acceptanceCriteria.given: the caller lacks PII_CONTACT/partition or searches a matching contact outside scope
acceptanceCriteria.then: raw contact and out-of-scope candidate existence are not exposed and unauthorized mutation commits nothing

acceptanceCriteria.given: an identical command is replayed or a link/merge races with another revision
acceptanceCriteria.then: one lead/link effect remains and conflict/replay returns stable evidence without losing either history

tests: Run the focused Gradle test selection with Testcontainers for PostgreSQL where persistence is involved.
Prove both the authorized path and action/partition/field-group denial path; retain the XML test report in Jira evidence.
Replay the same idempotency key and expected version and assert exactly one persisted business effect.
observability: Propagate correlation ID into audit and outbox records.
Emit bounded metrics for command result, state, dependency failures, retry count, and processing age without filenames, document contents, or PII.
Document a repair query for stuck work and a safe retry or terminal-resolution procedure.
definitionOfDone: Migration, application code, focused tests, and repository CI pass.
Contract behavior and stable error codes match the catalog and no cross-service database read is introduced.
Jira contains commit/PR, test report, denial evidence, replay evidence, and rollback/repair note.

issues.summary: [VS-E09] Billing, Deposits & VietQR Payments
issues.actor: Finance employee, payer, or payment operator
issues.outcome: Billing and payments are decomposed into Finance obligations/allocations/refunds, Payment provider intents/callbacks/reconciliation, installment schedules, Admin consumers and activation evidence.
issues.context: Historical delivered issues remain immutable; Stories and coordinating Tasks are non-dispatchable and only their executable repository leaves may be assigned.
inScope: Implement and verify: Billing, Deposits & VietQR Payments.
Version contract, persistence, authorization, failure, audit, and operator behavior needed by this outcome.
Provide repository-specific automated tests and Postman/Newman evidence for callable APIs.
outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.
Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: Advance payment is credited to the final or last receivable; it is neither a security deposit nor revenue at collection time.
Deposit is a configured percentage of eligible booking total after discounts and including staff markup, bounded by stay-type min/max, excluding incident/damage charges.
No production monetary default exists until maker-checker publication.
Provider confirmation is deduplicated and never directly rewrites Finance balances.
interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Finance owns charges, receivables, allocations, refunds, deposit obligations, and financial projections; Payment owns intents, QR payloads, provider transactions, callbacks, and technical reconciliation.
stateMachine: Model legal states and transitions for Billing, Deposits & VietQR Payments; reject illegal transitions with stable error codes.
Persist actor, reason, source, policy/contract version, expected revision, and timestamps for every material transition.
Terminal or superseded records are retained; corrections use a new revision or compensating record.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM for internal repair only; otherwise enforce the subject account type and the resource customer, host-party, site, branch, or assigned-employee partition.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; FINANCIAL, PII, DOCUMENT, TRUST_DETAIL, and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit grants and response-field filtering.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

acceptanceCriteria.then: the documented outcome, state revision, audit record, and contract response are produced deterministically

acceptanceCriteria.then: access is denied without leaking existence or restricted fields and the denial is auditable

Reserve provider order ID and idempotency before external QR generation; matching retry returns the same intent/presentation and changed payload returns IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH.
Honor DISABLED, GENERATE_ONLY and CALLBACK_ENABLED activation modes and quarantine ambiguous provider timeouts for safe retry/reconciliation.

issues.actor: Authorized backoffice operator or trusted ViStay service

inScope: Replace monetary bookingItems input with period ID, expectedVersion, source cutoff and idempotency key; load frozen Property term plus Finance collection/refund allocations and Booking service-date components through versioned service boundaries.

For MANAGEMENT, calculate basis from verified collected lodging after discounts/refunds; exclude unearned deposit, staff markup, damage, cleaning and employee commission; include OTA commission only when the effective term explicitly assigns it to the host settlement.

Require every staying person, including minors, exactly once; require exactly one responsible primary adult and reconcile active adult/child counts with the reservation snapshot before PRE_ARRIVAL_READY.
Resolve required items from the frozen policy version, occupant category, nationality and stay context; do not assume every minor needs the same document.
Expose idempotent roster upsert/remove, checklist query/complete and readiness query operations with expectedVersion, immutable audit/outbox and no raw identity/document fields.

Production credentials, destructive history rewrites, or silent fallback authorization.

issues.outcome: A deterministic Postman/Newman flow proves mapping, outbound ARI, inbound new/modify/cancel feed, ack order, reconciliation, dead-letter and repair across OTA and Booking.
issues.context: Use the local Channex mock from S05 and existing Keycloak/Postman environment conventions; never require a production Channex key or retain provider/card secrets in reports.
inScope: Add deterministic Property/Booking/OTA fixtures for one capacity-one SHORT unit, one Channex property/room/rate mapping and frozen dates/revisions.
Exercise connection test/activation, mapping, availability/rate publish, webhook trigger, oldest-first feed, new/modify/cancel apply, ack, reconciliation and authorized repair.

Assert wrong secret, non-SHORT/capacity-not-one, mapping collision, overlap, out-of-order/duplicate revision, card sanitization, ARI 200 warning, 401/429/timeout/5xx, retry exhaustion and cross-partition denial.
Provide seed/fault/webhook/run/reconcile/cleanup PowerShell runner producing redacted Newman JSON/JUnit plus database/provider-call evidence and safe repeatability.
outOfScope: Runtime business logic owned by another repository.
Production secrets or unapproved policy values.
Changing historical Jira workflow or bypassing the catalog readiness gate.
businessRules: Pilot mapping is one exact ViStay unit to one Channex Property and one Room Type with inventory one; pilot supports SHORT stays only.
Require current Channex HMAC verification in production; shared-secret fallback is sandbox-only.
Webhook is a trigger: pull Booking Revision Feed, durably apply in order, then acknowledge.
Out-of-order revisions, HTTP 429, and ARI warnings are handled; conflicts enter NEEDS_MANUAL_RESOLUTION and are never auto-cancelled or overwritten.
Do not ingest card or CVV data.
interfaces: Version every externally consumed operation or event and state its owner, caller, compatibility rule, timeout, and stable error behavior.
Keep fixtures deterministic and free of production credentials or customer data.
dataOwnership: This task owns only the named contract, UI, or infrastructure artifacts; authoritative domain rows remain in their service database.
stateMachine: Artifact lifecycle is DRAFT -> VALIDATED -> PUBLISHED; an incompatible semantic change requires a new version.
A failed validation remains unpublished and produces an actionable diagnostic.
Rollback selects the last validated artifact and does not mutate its contents.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM contract catalogue or the explicit ADMIN SITE/BRANCH partition used by the tested operation.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; DOCUMENT, PII, and INTERNAL_AUDIT appear only in explicitly granted test cases.

failureSemantics: Fail validation or startup when a required contract, environment value, or dependency is absent.
Never print tokens, presigned URLs, private document fields, or production values in test output.
Use stable assertion messages so a weak agent can locate the failing contract or scenario.
idempotencyConcurrency: Fixtures use unique deterministic business keys and cleanup is safe to repeat.
Repeated publication of identical canonical input produces the same fingerprint.
Concurrent API examples assert one effect or an explicit conflict.

acceptanceCriteria.given: clean local services, deterministic fixtures and Channex mock
acceptanceCriteria.then: mapping through ARI and new/modify/cancel feed/ack/reconciliation/repair paths pass with source/provider revision evidence

acceptanceCriteria.given: auth, pilot eligibility, mapping, overlap, order/replay, card, warning, provider failure, retry-limit or partition negative case
acceptanceCriteria.then: the exact stable error/redaction and absence of duplicate/partial/premature-ack effect are asserted

acceptanceCriteria.given: runner executes twice after cleanup/reseed
acceptanceCriteria.then: no duplicate mapping, ARI effect, reservation, inventory transition, ack, conflict or repair decision remains

tests: Run every exact command listed in testCases from the repository root.
Attach the machine-readable report plus a short mapping from each AC ID to its evidence.
Repeat the deterministic validation or flow and confirm no duplicate effect.
observability: Test output includes correlation ID and stable error code but no secrets or protected field values.
Operational artifacts include readiness/failure evidence and a rollback or cleanup note.
definitionOfDone: All named artifacts exist and repository CI passes.
Compatibility, authorization-negative, repeatability, and cleanup/rollback evidence are attached.
Catalog and Jira are synchronized and a selected DryRun returns zero changes.
evidence: Commit/PR and CI URL.
Machine-readable test or Newman report.
Compatibility and rollback/cleanup note.
Jira zero-diff synchronization result.

issues.summary: [VS-E15] Cutover & Pilot Readiness
issues.actor: Pilot release manager
issues.outcome: Pilot readiness is decomposed into all-database recovery, owner-safe minimum-data migration/reconciliation, guarded rehearsal/rollback/sign-off, pilot-wide observability/incident drills and externally gated VietQR callback activation.
issues.context: Technical tooling is dispatchable; real dataset execution and named approvals remain activation-gated by VS-E00-S07. Full history, cross-service database access and production HA are outside this epic.
inScope: Implement and verify: Cutover & Pilot Readiness.
Version contract, persistence, authorization, failure, audit, and operator behavior needed by this outcome.
Provide repository-specific automated tests and Postman/Newman evidence for callable APIs.
outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.
Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: Cutover requires encrypted backup plus restore smoke before forward migration.
Every migrated aggregate has count, key, amount, and exception reconciliation.
Public callback activation requires HTTPS, provider UAT, secrets, alerting, and rollback evidence.
interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Each service owns its migration and reconciliation evidence; infrastructure owns orchestration, backup, restore, and rollback runbooks.
stateMachine: Model legal states and transitions for Cutover & Pilot Readiness; reject illegal transitions with stable error codes.
Persist actor, reason, source, policy/contract version, expected revision, and timestamps for every material transition.
Terminal or superseded records are retained; corrections use a new revision or compensating record.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM for internal repair only; otherwise enforce the subject account type and the resource customer, host-party, site, branch, or assigned-employee partition.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; FINANCIAL, PII, DOCUMENT, TRUST_DETAIL, and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit grants and response-field filtering.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an authorized actor with a valid partition and a complete request for Cutover & Pilot Readiness
acceptanceCriteria.when: the command or query is executed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the documented outcome, state revision, audit record, and contract response are produced deterministically

acceptanceCriteria.given: a caller missing the action, partition, or requested field-group grant
acceptanceCriteria.then: access is denied without leaking existence or restricted fields and the denial is auditable

acceptanceCriteria.given: the same mutation is replayed or two requests use the same expected revision
acceptanceCriteria.then: at most one business effect is committed and all responses are stable, explainable, and reconciled

tests: Unit tests cover rule boundaries, legal/illegal transitions, rounding/timezone where relevant, and stable error mapping.
Integration tests cover persistence constraints, authorization action+partition+field groups, outbox/inbox replay, and dependency failure.
Postman/Newman flow covers happy path, negative authorization, validation, conflict, idempotent replay, and a cleanup-safe deterministic fixture.
observability: Propagate trace and correlation IDs across GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/webhook boundaries without logging secrets or protected fields.
Emit transition, latency, error-code, replay/deduplication, dependency, and repair-queue metrics with bounded-cardinality labels.
Provide dashboard/alert thresholds and a runbook for stuck states, reconciliation mismatch, and rollback.
definitionOfDone: Catalog validation and all affected repository CI checks pass.
Contracts, migrations, compatibility path, implementation, Admin Web/Mobile parity where applicable, and Postman/Newman evidence are merged.
Security-negative, concurrency/replay, observability, reconciliation, and rollback evidence is linked in Jira.
No production secret or unapproved monetary/policy default is committed; ServiceOwner acceptance evidence is attached before Done.
evidence: Pull request and commit links per repository.
Automated test and Newman report with fixture version.
Migration/rollback or compatibility evidence where data/contracts change.
Dashboard, trace, audit, and reconciliation screenshots or machine-readable artifacts.
issues.decisionNoteVi: Các quy tắc nghiệp vụ và ranh giới dữ liệu trong catalog v1.2 đã được chốt; thay đổi sau này phải tạo phiên bản policy/contract mới, không sửa ngược lịch sử.

issues.actor: Authenticated internal source consumer for ingestion; authorized reporting viewer/operator for analytical reads and repair.
issues.outcome: Warehouse derives versioned Booking, Property, masked Customer, channel and eligible property-night analytical rows from validated owner events without overwriting historical corrections.
issues.context: V2 already declares fact_bookings, fact_property_nights and SCD2 dim_property; current consumer fills booking facts but does not populate property-night denominators and can substitute zero/unspecified status/HOURLY legacy defaults.
inScope: Map canonical E08 booking statuses and E04 eligibility revisions to dim_property as-of keys and fact_bookings; require explicit stay type and complete authoritative amount snapshot.

Materialize one property_id/service_date eligible/occupied row from owner availability/booking facts with property-local date boundaries and explicit off-market reason; do not infer denominator only from booked nights.

Retain source event/revision, point-in-time customer masking, channel and staff attribution references; no email, phone, token, raw guest name or current-row-only join to rewrite historical property data.
Quarantine missing property eligibility, overlapping occupancy, invalid date/amount or legacy HOURLY instead of fabricating saleable nights.
outOfScope: Frontend rendering outside the owning service contract.
Direct reads from another service database.
Production credentials, destructive history rewrites, or silent fallback authorization.
businessRules: Ingestion is replayable, deduplicated, schema-version aware, and reconciled to source control totals.
PII is minimized and dashboard/export authorization applies action, partition, and field group.
interfaces: Consume only allow-listed versioned owner events or authenticated source snapshots; never read another service database.

issues.actor: ViStay SRE, architecture reviewer or release operator
issues.outcome: Contracts gives approvers one reproducible service-level register with measured and target fields, precise owners, risk acceptance and activation gates, without inventing target values.
issues.context: E22 baseline requires versioned SLO, RTO, RPO, capacity and cost before production HA. Existing Compose service health checks are not SLO or DR evidence.
inScope: Define per-critical-journey availability/latency/error-budget measurement for sign-in, inventory/quote, booking confirmation, Finance collection and customer/admin reads with trace and denominator semantics.

Record baseline sample window, peak/steady traffic, DB sizes, events/lag, currency/booking data criticality, geographic failure domains, projected capacity and cost; distinguish measured observations from proposed/approved targets.

Require ProductOwner/SRE approval fingerprint and effective date for target SLO, RTO, RPO, maximum data loss, maintenance policy and budget; unresolved fields produce NOT_APPROVED and block HA activation.
Add valid/invalid fixtures for zero denominator, mixed service durations, unapproved cost, missing RPO, impossible replica quorum and mistaken single-node HA claim.
outOfScope: Publishing numeric production targets or paid infrastructure capacity without owner approval.
businessRules: SLO, RTO, RPO, capacity assumptions, failure domains, and cost envelope are versioned before HA implementation.
A backup is not accepted until an isolated restore and application-level reconciliation pass.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM deployment and approved SRE/DBA roles only; SITE/BRANCH domain data remains scoped by its service even during failover.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY targets/status; INTERNAL_AUDIT cost, production topology and approvers restricted.

failureSemantics: Fail closed on missing approved capacity/SLO, failover quorum, authentication, secret references or valid restore evidence; never label a local single-node smoke run as production HA.

idempotencyConcurrency: Recovery tests replay outbox/inbox events and compare business keys so Booking inventory, Payment/Finance money and Notifications remain at-most-once in effect.

outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.

businessRules: SLO, RTO, RPO, capacity assumptions, failure domains, and cost envelope are versioned before HA implementation.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.

issues.outcome: Infrastructure proves repeatable encrypted backup and isolated PITR/Keycloak recovery with off-site failure-domain evidence and never restores over live data.
issues.context: One local Postgres volume, Kafka volume and Redis AOF are not a backup plan; no production off-site storage or RPO has been approved.
inScope: Prepare inactive-by-default backup/restore templates for service and Keycloak Postgres using WAL/point-in-time recovery, Kafka retention/checkpoint, encrypted artifact/checksum and recoverable key reference.
